title: Circular phonon dichroism in $d$-wave altermagnets
authors: Ding Li, Tao Qin, Jianhui Zhou
abstract: Altermagnets, a new class of collinear antiferromagnets, exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting and offer compelling advantages for antiferromagnetic spintronics. However, the magnetic order is intrinsically difficult to read out, which hinders practical applications. We propose finite-momentum circular phonon dichroism as a direct probe of Néel vector in two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnets. Combining Onsager reciprocity with $C_{2z}$ lattice symmetry, we find that the dichroic signal reverses sign when the Néel vector is flipped for the in-plane phonon wave vectors. Moreover, a channel-resolved decomposition identifies the circular phonon dichroism originates from the interband coherent transitions. Representative finite-momentum cuts show pronounced dichroic asymmetric ratio, with $|η_{\mathrm{CPD}}|=37.3\%$. Our work reveals that the circular-ultrasound absorption acts as a direct probe of the Néel vector of $d$-wave altermagnets.
summary: The authors propose using finite-momentum circular phonon dichroism (CPD) as a highly sensitive and direct diagnostic tool to determine the orientation of the Néel vector in $d$-wave altermagnets. By exploiting symmetry constraints, they show that CPD's sign reverses when the magnetic order is reversed, offering a practical acoustic method for characterizing these complex antiferromagnetic materials.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a direct, measurable technique to determine the orientation of the Néel vector ($\mathbf{N}$) in altermagnets because their magnetic order is otherwise difficult to read out.
main_result: Finite-momentum circular phonon dichroism (CPD) acts as a direct and sign-sensitive probe for the Néel vector, showing that the signal reverses when $\mathbf{N}$ is flipped.
method: The theory calculates CPD by analyzing the difference between left ($\gamma_L$) and right ($\gamma_R$) circular ultrasound amplitudes, relating it to the Hall-like component of the electron-phonon coupling tensor ($\eta_{	ext{CPD}} = -\gamma_A / \gamma_D$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on two-dimensional ($d$-wave) altermagnets. The electronic structure is modeled using a minimal two-band Hamiltonian incorporating $d$-wave exchange splitting ($J$) and Rashba spin-orbit coupling ($\lambda$).
key_observables: Circular phonon dichroism asymmetry ratio ($\eta_{	ext{CPD}}$), which is expected to change sign upon Néel vector reversal.
important_parameters: The magnitude of the dichroic signal, exemplified by $|\eta_{	ext{CPD}}| = 37.3\%$, and the dependence on phonon wave vectors ($q$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on combining Onsager reciprocity with $C_{2z}$ lattice symmetry to predict the sign change of CPD upon Néel vector reversal.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate the concept by showing unequal transmitted amplitudes ($\gamma_L 
eq \gamma_R$) for opposite $\mathbf{N}$ orientations, and quantify the dichroic asymmetry ratio across various momentum cuts.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a theoretical framework using electron-phonon coupling to define CPD. It derives symmetry constraints based on crystal and time-reversal symmetries, calculates the signal originating from interband transitions, and presents quantitative results confirming its utility as an orientation probe.
why_interesting: This work connects macroscopic acoustic measurements (ultrasound) directly to microscopic magnetic order parameters ($\mathbf{N}$), providing a novel, non-magnetic readout mechanism relevant for spintronics applications in correlated materials.
